acceptance_criteria.criterion: ADR-009 is committed and specifies the encoding bit-for-bit, including framing, tags, ordering, representations, collections, supported types, collisions, and rejection cases.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: ADR-009 says plain objects are supported but only enumerable properties are encoded. It neither excludes nor rejects non-enumerable own properties, and §6 nevertheless claims logically distinct states cannot share an encoding.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: packages/core exports canonicalEncode(state, encodingVersion) returning Uint8Array and CanonicalEncoderError.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: packages/core/src/index.ts exports CanonicalEncoderError and canonicalEncode(state: unknown, encodingVersion: string): Uint8Array.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Logically equal supported states with different object insertion orders encode identically.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Object keys are recursively sorted by UTF-8 bytes; focused root and nested insertion-order tests pass.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tested logically distinct states encode differently, including numeric type, nesting, collection kind, and framing distinctions.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The candidate explicitly tests that a plain object with an additional non-enumerable accessor is accepted and ignored. Likewise, an enumerable property and an otherwise identical non-enumerable data property can produce identical bytes despite being distinct admitted object states.
encodingVersion is length-framed in the envelope and two version-separation tests pass.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Undefined, invalid numbers, cycles, and ADR-excluded value types throw CanonicalEncoderError.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Implementation provides dedicated rejection paths and the supplied suite covers required invalid values plus excluded object and collection forms.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Unordered collections are insertion-order independent; ordered collections preserve order.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Objects and Sets are sorted canonically; Arrays and Maps retain order. Corresponding tests pass.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No StateHash, SaveHash, RNG, ledger, world, application, or Electron implementation is introduced.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Candidate changes are limited to the encoder, ADR, tests, test-script inclusion, and core module metadata.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Repository typecheck, lint, architecture-boundary checks, and complete test suite pass.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Automated validation confirms lint and 125 tests, including boundary tests, but explicitly warns that no typecheck script was run. The implementer reports npm run compile passed but supplies only a summary rather than captured command output.

findings.evidence: encodeObject obtains all own names but executes `if (descriptor === undefined || descriptor.enumerable !== true) continue;`. The test `acceptance: non-enumerable accessor descriptors are ignored` codifies this omission. Thus `{a: 1n}` and an object with the same enumerable property plus any non-enumerable own property encode identically, even though both pass the plain-object admissibility check. This conflicts with the ADR's injectivity and collision claims and with the task's distinct-state requirement.
findings.required_change: Define non-enumerable own properties as unsupported in ADR-009 and reject them with CanonicalEncoderError before encoding, or normatively define and implement an injective representation for them. Replace the test that accepts ignored non-enumerable properties with rejection or distinction coverage.
findings.title: Non-enumerable plain-object state is silently discarded

findings.evidence: The automated validation ran install, diff-check, lint, and tests, then warned `No 'typecheck' script is currently defined.` It did not run `npm run compile`. The implementer report asserts compile succeeded but provides no captured stdout/stderr or automated result supporting that assertion.
findings.required_change: Run and capture `npm run compile` against the final corrected candidate, with exit code 0, alongside boundary, lint, and the complete test suite.
findings.title: Required typecheck validation lacks independently verifiable output

invariants_checked: Core contains no dependencies on world, domain, application, adapters, UI, or Electron packages.
No state hash, save hash, RNG, ledger, world, application, or Electron implementation was introduced.
Object and Set ordering avoid insertion-order dependence for encoded logical entries.
Array and Map ordering remains significant.
Encoding uses explicit tags, big-endian lengths, and version framing.
Invalid numeric values, cycles, unsupported values, accessors, and collection collisions have dedicated errors.
No time, randomness, locale collation, native hashing, or platform-endian encoding is used.
Existing lint and test validation remains green.
risks: Silently omitted non-enumerable properties can cause distinct runtime state graphs to share canonical bytes and therefore undermine any future StateHash or SaveHash built on this encoder.
The unverified compile step leaves a required repository-level validation gap.
payload.summary: The encoder largely implements the requested format, but it admits plain objects with non-enumerable own properties while silently omitting those properties, allowing distinct admitted states to share bytes. Required typecheck validation is also not independently evidenced by the automated output.
